name: vq2_dark_red_negatives
description: HARD NEGATIVES in the vq2_dark_red domain: on-course viewpoints with NO gate, dressed with gate-COLOURED non-gate shapes (billboards, angled slabs, discs) and tiled/grid ceilings (white grid, ceiling tiles, dark garage tiles, panel grid). Empty labels. WHY: M+1 trained on 4000 frames with ZERO negatives and hallucinates CONFIDENTLY -- on held-out gate-free frames its median false-positive score is 0.574 against M's 0.293, and its p90 false positive (0.841) outscores its own MEDIAN true positive (0.832), so no detection threshold can separate them. M had 13.1% negatives, 180 of them the purpose-built vq2_confuser corpus. That corpus is unusable here for two reasons: it predates the dark-red domain fix (bright AgX look, background median gray ~104 vs real 37), and it was rendered on the LEGACY path via build_background/background_material, which no photoreal preset ever executes. So the confusers had to be rebuilt on the photoreal path -- otherwise a dark-red negative contains no red at all, and red panels are precisely what the false positives fire on. APPEARANCE IS COPIED VERBATIM from vq2_dark_red (same HDRI set, same ambient_strength_range, same exposure_range, same Standard view transform) because a negative that does not share the positives' domain teaches the detector to separate BRIGHTNESS, not shape. The only deliberate viewpoint change is a wider pitch jitter, so the camera looks UP into the ceiling grids often enough for them to matter.
